focuses on creating intelligent machines that can perform tasks that
typically require human intelligence.
Real-world applications

and respond to voice commands.

suggest products or content based on user preferences.
Autonomous vehicles: Self-driving cars use AI to navigate roads and
obey traffic laws.

assist doctors in detecting diseases.
Types of AI
Narrow AI: Designed to perform a specific task (e.g.
voice recognition).
General AI: Hypothetical AI with human-level cognitive abilities across all domains.
Superintelligence: AI that surpasses human intelligence in all aspects.

modules.title: Core AI Concepts and Technologies
modules.text:
Some Complex Topics:
If you are interested to learn more about AI you must learn the following 5 concepts:
Neural Networks:
- A system of connected nodes arranged in layers that process data
- Data goes in one end, flows through layers, and a result comes out
- Training adjusts internal weights each time the model gets something wrong
- After enough training it handles examples it has never seen before
- All modern AI — LLMs, image generators, voice models — are neural networks
Frontier Models vs Open source models:
- Frontier models are the most powerful proprietary models (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini)
- Accessed via API and charged per use; weights are kept private by the company
- Open source models have publicly released weights (Llama, Mistral, Qwen).
The models
used by the PhillipCapital chgatbot is open source.
- Open source gives full control and can be cheaper at scale but needs own infrastructure
- Choice depends on capability needed, control required, and budget
Embedding Model:
- Converts text (or images, audio) into a list of numbers called a vector
- Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together in numerical space
- "Dog" and "puppy" will be close; "dog" and "skyscraper" will be far apart
- Turns unstructured language into something computers can compare mathematically
- Foundation of search, recommendations, and any "find similar content" feature
Cosine Similarity:
- Measures how similar two vectors are by calculating the angle between them
- Score of 1.0 = identical meaning; -1.0 = opposite; 0 = unrelated
- Uses angle not straight-line distance — unaffected by length of text
- Used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query
Vector database
- A database built to store embeddings and search through them at speed
- Returns the closest matching vectors to a query — called nearest neighbour search
- Unlike SQL, finds fuzzy meaning-based matches rather than exact keyword matches
- Popular options: Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector
- The backbone of any RAG system connecting AI to your private documents

engine.

how those numbers get compared.
A vector database is where they get stored and searched.
And understanding the difference between frontier and open source models tells you which
engine to pick for any job.
Once these click, the intermediate concepts — RAG, agents, transformers, orchestration —
become much easier to understand because they are all just these five ideas combined in
different ways.
That is what the next module covers.

You are a course curriculum designer. You will receive the body content of a training document.
Each line of the document has been pre-numbered in the format: [LINE N] <content>
Your task is to segment the entire content into high-level course modules.

MODULE COUNT:
- You MUST create between 3 and 6 modules for the entire document.
- Do NOT output only 1 or 2 modules for the entire document unless it is extremely short (less than 2 pages).
- Only exceed 6 modules if the document EXPLICITLY defines more via clearly labeled chapters, modules, or major section headings in the source text (e.g. "Module 1:", "Chapter 3:", "Part II:").

- Foundation of search, recommendations, and any "find similar content" feature

- Used in vector search to find the most relevant content for a query

- Returns the closest matching vectors to a query — called nearest neighbour search
